The cardiovascular system is made up of:
A/ The heart: it is a motor organ which allows the propulsion of blood in the vessels.
1- Arteries: these are conduits that distribute oxygen, food and hormones to tissues.
2- The veins: collect CO2 and waste.
3- Capillaries: These are the places where exchanges between blood and tissues take place.
C/The lymphatic vessels: transport of a large part of the fats coming from the diet towards the circulation, transport of waste, germs and damaged cells.

pages.title: The interstitial fluid circulating in the lymphatic vessels is called lymph

blocks.text: The interstitial fluid circulating in the lymphatic vessels is called lymph.
Lymph comes from the blood, accumulates in the interstitial sector and then circulates in the lymphatic vessels.
The lymphatic system intervenes in the body's defense process by allowing defense cells to circulate throughout the body and thus activate the so-called specific immune response.

blocks.text: The heart is irrigated by two main coronary arteries (right and left) which arise from the aorta.

Their divisions run at the level of the epicardium and direct perpendicularly arranged “perforating arteries” towards the myocardium. These, taking a longitudinal orientation and are distributed in a network of arteries “terminal arterioles”; each branch of which serves a specific region.
The total obstruction of a branch leads to the cessation of traffic in the region served by this branch. Necrosis or myocardial infarction MI is the result of this ischemia.
Partial obstruction of the coronary arteries reduces the supply of O2 and causes pain: ANGOR.
The heart is innervated by both sympathetic fibers which increase the heart rate
and by parasympathetic fibers which slow it down.
Sensitive fibers (sensitivity + pain) are present in the pericardium and the endocardium
At the level of the epicardium of the posterior surface of the atria, there are nerve cells organized into plexuses (sino atrial plexus, atrio ventricular plexus).

These neurons operate semi-autonomously from the brain (receive information from the brain but also from mechanical and chemical sensors located at the heart). They adjust in real time the heart rate, the force of contraction and the conduction of nerve impulses.

blocks.text: Depending on their location in the arterial and venous vascular territory, capillary networks are classified into 3 categories:
1- The capillary network: interposed between an arteriole and a venule.
2- The arterial portal network: interposed between two arterioles (kidney).
3- The portal venous network: interposed between two Venules (liver).
